title: Early OA

positions.as_written: Take the history: the pain on load, the stiffness after sitting, the swelling after activity, and how far the patient walks before stopping.
Assess the effusion, because a recurrent activity related effusion is the sign most often present when the radiograph is still near normal.
Measure the range both ways, since the first loss in early wear is the last few degrees of flexion rather than extension.
Assess the quadriceps, because the bulk and the ability to hold the leg straight reflect how long the knee has been avoided.
